resources.string: Use a key from a phone
Key from a phone
Scan this code with TailSocks on your phone

The scanner is in the top bar of the app\'s main screen. The phone and the TV must be on the same Wi-Fi or wired network; a VPN on the phone can get in the way. The phone asks for an auth key and sends it here encrypted. Nothing is used until you confirm it on this screen.

The TV shows the same name and address beside its code. If they differ, the code you scanned is not that TV\'s: do not send.
Auth key

An auth key from your tailnet\'s admin console (Settings → Keys), or a Headscale pre-auth key. A one-time, pre-approved key is the safest: this TV uses it up. It goes straight to the TV over the local network, encrypted, and is neither shown again nor kept on this phone.
Paste
The clipboard has no text
An auth key has no spaces: only Latin letters, digits and punctuation.
Too long for an auth key.
This is an API access token. A TV needs an auth key.
Does not look like a Tailscale or Headscale key. It will be sent as it is.
Login server (optional)
Only for a key from a server of your own, such as Headscale. Left empty, the TV\'s server stays as it is.
A server address looks like https://example.com
Sending the key to the TV…
Make sure the TV shows the same code, then confirm there.
If the TV shows another code, a key from someone else got there first: reject it on the TV. Never confirm on the TV a code you do not see here.

The phone and the TV must be on the same Wi-Fi or wired network. A VPN on this phone can get in the way, and guest networks often keep devices apart.

The TV closed its code
The screen with the code went away before anyone answered, and the TV discarded the key.
Connection lost
The key reached the TV, but its answer did not come back. The TV\'s screen shows how it ended.
The TV already holds a key
Another device sent one first, so yours was not taken. If that was not you, reject the key on the TV.
The TV cannot use this
Its TailSocks is another version. Update the app on both devices.
